item.title: Tech with Mak Writing ML code is one thing. Figuring out how to make the next AI
item.description:
Tech with Mak
Writing ML code is one thing. Figuring out how to make the next AI model better is an entirely different challenge.

Imagine giving an AI agent one task: "Improve the training optimizer."

No implementation plan. It must identify promising approaches, design experiments, compare baselines, and demonstrate measurable improvements.

That's the kind of open-ended research FrontierRSI evaluates, covering pre-training, post-training, inference, agent harnesses, and GPU kernels.

If AI agents can reliably do this, they could contribute directly to the research that builds their own successors.

That's what makes this direction of recursive self-improvement research so interesting.

Introducing FrontierRSI, a new recursive self-improvement benchmark by @abundant_labs.

We evaluate agents on (1) a broad range of AI research and engineering work, and (2) post-training models on multi-step agentic tasks, rather than single-step tasks as in PostTrainBench. https://t.co/s1lG4lb2aP - Kevin Lin
tweet

item.title: World of Statistics Deadly antibiotic-resistant “superbug” surging in European h
item.description:
World of Statistics
Deadly antibiotic-resistant “superbug” surging in European hospitals, per Politico & ECDC.

Bloodstream infections from drug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae jumped 72% between 2019–2025 (EU target was a 5% cut by 2030). Mortality in serious cases typically 40–70%. Some strains now resist nearly all antibiotics, including newer ones.
It’s mainly a hospital-acquired threat that spreads between patients. ECDC calls it the biggest concern in this year’s superbug data.

item.title: Eric Xing RT @IFM_AI : Several world model releases in a few months, and still n
item.description:
Eric Xing
RT @IFM_AI: Several world model releases in a few months, and still not sure what a world model is for?

Here's one answer: it lets you ask "what if I try this?" and see the answer.

An LLM can tell you how to climb a route. It can't show you whether you'll make the reach.
PAN 2 does both, from one photo of the wall. 🧗

It’s made possible by two reasoners working together:
• Conceptual reasoner: plans the climb in words. Which holds to use, and which hand moves next on this route.
• Perceptual reasoner: shows visually on the wall the details the plan doesn't spell out: hips, reach, weight shift, timing. They decide whether the climb succeeds or fails.

👇 Concept demo. All climbing footage is generated by PAN 2.

Try PAN 2: https://t.co/Lm1F4rEolT
tweet
